verdict_text:
YES

The plan deletes the 48 buffers first (so the blanket `float32` cast never touches the uint8 mask), casts everything remaining to float32, then casts exactly the 64 projection matrices to bfloat16, leaving names untouched and 196 tensors. The two dtype asserts partition the whole name space — the projection regex and its negative-lookahead complement — so together they enforce "exactly 64 bfloat16, everything else float32", and the remaining asserts cover the qkv/embed_in dtypes and the 196-tensor count, all before the write. Output goes to `out/T3` as sharded safetensors with a 256 MiB budget, which puts each 412 MB float32 embedding matrix in a shard of its own and emits the index file.
